title: Ordinary ringed pullback agrees with completed integral pullback on constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, and $t$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Here noetherian means locally noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and finite-dimensional means that lengths of strict chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets have a finite bound. No separatedness or linearity over a base field is assumed. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_W=\varprojlim_n(R/t^n)_W$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ be the ring-sheaf map whose composite with the $n$-th projection is $c^f_{R/t^n}\circ f^{-1}(\pi_n)$, using the constant coefficient structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The categories $D(B_W)$ are the ordinary unbounded derived categories of sheaves of $B_W$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_f:D(B_Y)\to D(B_X)$ for ordinary ringed-topos derived pullback,
$$P_fK=B_X\otimes^L_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}K,$$
as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and $\widehat P_f$ for the completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For $K\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the object $P_fK$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$ and the canonical completion comparison
$$\eta_{f,K}:P_fK\longrightarrow\widehat P_fK$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$. This is the following specified map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of the endpoints. For a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{B_Y}(R/t^n)_Y$. The coefficient quotient maps give compatible chain maps
$$f^*_{B}Q\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_n f_n^*Q_n,$$
where $f^*_{B}Q=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}Q$, $f_n^*$ is finite-coefficient module pullback and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ restricts the action to $B_X$. Their product is killed by $1-s$, for the actual quotient transitions. The map to the strict-tower derived-limit model $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ has these quotient maps in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product. It represents $\eta_{f,K}$ under the K-flat and strict-tower identifications. The resulting derived map is independent of the resolution under its canonical comparison isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 (stratified perfect characterization), Lemma 6.5.9 (completed pullback), and Remark 6.8.15 (ordinary ringed coefficient functors restrict to the constructible six functors), pp. 50, 54, 62; explicit quotient-cone normalization is an agent formulation of the canonical completion map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to $K$ on $Y$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given coefficient, noetherianity, dimension and invertibility hypotheses. The noetherian convention agrees: quasi-compactness extracts a finite subcover from the noetherian affine neighbourhoods provided by local noetherianity. The last comparison sentence of that lemma applies to the category in this item, not just to a category with similar notation. Obtain a finite constructible locally closed stratification $Y=\coprod_i S_i$ and pro-etale covers of $S_i$ on which $K|_{S_i}$ is the completed scalar extension of a perfect $R$-complex. Choose bounded finite-projective representatives $L^\bullet$ for these local models.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward direction; comparison to the DAG integral category supplied by the cited characterization

proof.text: Put $X_i=X\times_Y S_i$ and discard empty strata. These form a finite stratification of $X$ in [def-constructible-stratification]. Indeed an immersion factors into a closed immersion into an open subscheme: inverse image of that open is open, and on affine charts the closed part $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ pulls back to $\operatorname{Spec}(C/JC)$, since $C\otimes_A(A/J)=C/JC$. Its image is the inverse image of the original stratum, so the images remain disjoint and cover $X$. Each is locally closed, hence constructible on the noetherian space $X$. For the latter assertion, every open in a noetherian space is quasi-compact and a locally closed subset is the intersection of an open with a closed subset, which is the constructible convention here. For each trivializing cover $\{U_a\to S_i\}$, the family $\{X_i\times_{S_i}U_a\to X_i\}$ is a pro-etale cover: this is the covering-preserving base-change assertion of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](1).

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Remark 6.8.15: elementary base-change construction of the stratification and covers

proof.text:
Write $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i_i:S_i\hookrightarrow Y$, and $f_i:X_i\to S_i$. The ringed morphisms for $f j_i=i_i f_i$ agree: after projection to $(R/t^n)_{X_i}$ both structural maps send a constant residue to the same residue, and equality into $B_{X_i}$ is equality after all its limit projections. The composition comparison in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] therefore gives
$$j_i^*P_fK\simeq P_{f_i}(i_i^*K).$$
Here ordinary immersion pullback is exact and is the restriction functor, by [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison]; this use is of its ordinary exactness assertion, without presupposing completeness of $P_fK$. Restrict this equality to the covers in step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], ordinary derived pullback on each cover is the pullback between the localized ringed sites. On a local model it is
$$B_V\otimes_{f_i^{-1}B_{S_i}}f_i^{-1}(B_{S_i}\otimes_R L^\bullet)\cong B_V\otimes_R L^\bullet.$$
This calculation computes derived pullback: every term of the model is a direct summand of a finite free coefficient module, and its complex is bounded. Under the monoidal unit and composition comparisons of the first cited lemma, a free basis vector goes to the same basis vector; applying the corresponding idempotent gives the same assertion for each projective summand. Thus $P_fK$ has the required perfect local models on every $X_i$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] on $X$ to the perfect models just computed. It gives $M=P_fK\in D^b_c(X,R)$ with the definition of this item, including its uniform reduction bound. It also gives membership in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], hence intrinsic derived $(t)$-completeness in the precise Koszul-unit sense of that category. This last conclusion, rather than an arbitrary lift into a distinguished triangle, is what will establish invertibility of the specified completion map.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse direction; retain the intrinsic completion unit via the cited category comparison

proof.text:
Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ in the statement, and put $F=f_B^*Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $F$ represents $M$; by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], $F$ is itself K-flat with flat terms. Let $D_n=(R/t^n)_X$ and $C_n=(R/t^n)_Y$. The finite constant structure map $f^{-1}C_n\cong D_n$ and exact finite module pullback are those of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The exact monoidal inverse image of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] preserves the balanced tensor presentations (relative tensor is a cokernel of the two action maps). Consequently there are actual isomorphisms of complexes
$$h_n:F\otimes_{B_X}D_n\xrightarrow{\sim} f_n^*(Q\otimes_{B_Y}C_n).$$
In local balanced section notation they send $(b\otimes q)\otimes a$ to $1\otimes(q\otimes\pi_n(b)a)$. Both sides identify with $f^{-1}Q\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}D_n$; the inverse sends $1\otimes(q\otimes a)$ to $(1\otimes q)\otimes a$. These formulas are balanced and respect differentials. Under $D_{n+1}\to D_n$ both paths send a generator to $1\otimes(q\otimes\pi_n(b)\overline a)$, so $h_\bullet$ is an isomorphism of strict towers with their actual quotient transitions. It carries the quotient arrow $F\to F\otimes_{B_X}D_n$ to exactly the quotient arrow in the statement.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); explicit tensor reassociation for the quotient maps

proof.text: The adic hypotheses for [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] hold with $A=R$, $I=(t)$: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $R$ a principal ideal domain, hence noetherian, with $t$ nonzero; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] gives finite quotients. The residue is torsion since it is finite. For every $n\geq1$, $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is a finite free resolution of $R/t^n$, proving perfectness. Thus the intrinsic completeness of $M$ in step 4 implies that its canonical quotient-tower completion unit is an isomorphism, by [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]. Compute this unit using $F$ from step 5. Exact products and the strict Roos model in [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] identify its target with the cone of $1-s$ on $\prod_n(F\otimes_{B_X}D_n)$. The strict tower isomorphism $h_\bullet$ induces the product map in both cone coordinates. Since it carries each quotient map to the one in the statement, it carries the chain map having quotient maps in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product to that very specified chain map for $\eta_{f,K}$. Its target is $\widehat P_fK$ by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Hence $\eta_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism. This identifies chain maps of strict cones, not merely their projections in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), with Tag 0A0E (algebraization-lemma-derived-completion-koszul); explicit quotient-cone normalization

proof.text:
For a chain map $v:Q\to Q'$ between flat-term K-flat complexes, the equality
$$(f_n^*(v\otimes1))\,a_{n,Q}=a_{n,Q'}\,f_B^*(v)$$
holds on a generator $b\otimes q$: both expressions are $1\otimes(v(q)\otimes\pi_n(b))$. Taking products and placing zero in the other cone coordinate gives a strictly commuting square of the displayed comparison maps. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] assert that both representative constructions invert quasi-isomorphisms in this resolving class and give their canonical comparison isomorphisms on the derived category. The square therefore descends after localization, and also commutes with inverses of those quasi-isomorphisms. It proves naturality in $K$ and independence of $Q$ under the canonical comparisons for any two resolutions. All maps of schemes used above were arbitrary; no separatedness or base-field linearity was used.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); strict naturality of quotient maps and the cone construction
